title: Metric prefixes and decibels
blurb: Convert between milli, kilo, mega and other prefixes by moving the decimal, and tell dB from the power ratio.

T5B01.why: Milli is a thousandth, so there are 1000 mA in an ampere: 1.5 × 1000 = **1500 mA**.
T5B01.trap: Dividing makes a tiny number. A smaller unit needs a bigger number.

T5B02.trap: 1500 MHz would be a thousand times too large. Count the steps.

T5B03.why: Kilo means a thousand, so one kilovolt is **1000 volts**.
T5B03.trap: One thousandth of a volt is a millivolt.

T5B04.why: Micro means one millionth: one microvolt is **one-millionth of a volt**.
T5B04.trap: One thousandth of a volt is a millivolt.

T5B05.trap: Multiplying gives 500,000 W, which is wildly too big.

T5B06.trap: 0.003 A divides by 1,000,000. Only one rung separates milli from base.

T5B07.why: Mega to kilo is one rung down: 3.525 × 1000 = **3525 kHz**.
T5B07.trap: Going to the smaller unit makes the number bigger, not smaller.

T5B08.why: Pico to micro is two rungs up: 1,000,000 ÷ 1,000,000 = **1 µF**.
T5B08.trap: 0.001 µF is only 1000 pF. Pico to micro is two rungs (six places), not three.

T5B09.why: Power doubled (5 → 10 W). A doubling is **+3 dB**.
T5B09.trap: dB is about the ratio, not the 5 watts added.

T5B10.trap: −3 dB is only one halving (12 → 6 W).

T5B12.trap: 28.4 kHz misses a rung: 28,400 kHz is a thousand times larger.

T5B13.trap: MHz to GHz is one rung (÷1000). 0.002425 divides by a million.
